body.x: Headong Engineering will participate in theworld’s largest technology exhibition CES 2020 opening in Las Vegas on Jan.7-10 to showcase its Magnetic Flux Leakage (MFL) sensors and applications.

Haedong Engineering was established in 1990 and started electrician dispatching business and with the collaboration with ABB in Europe, it has grown to supply and construct cold rolled steel sheet shape control equipment. It established a technology institute In 2016 and began development of MFL sensors, and is developing next-generation measurement equipment to meet Industrial Revolution 4:0.

MFL inspection developed by Haedong Engineering is one of the non-destructive testing of defects on or near the surface, and it detects the crack leakage magnetic flux when the specimen is magnetized. It can be applied to inspection of defects of less than 3mm from the surface.

It successfully completed the developmentof thick plate defect detection system as a MSS project and commercialized it.It is also showing 90% progress in the development of the steel plate internaldefect detection system.

Major features are as follows. △ Imageconversion of magnetic field signal △ Can detect defects on the surface and upto 3 mm inside △ Canreplace vision sensor in bad environment with high humidityand low vision △ Pre-processing analysis by using detection informationidentification with machine learning

The official said, “We will introduce new contents every year, and we plan to expand it to various business groups with the brand obtained through this. We will participate in various domestic and international exhibitions and try to expand our share in the export and domestic markets. The main target countries are the US and Europe, and also the emerging markets in Southeast Asia.”

The world’s largest IT show CES shows the trend of the global consumer electronics industry at a glance. It is hosted by Consumer Technology Association (CTA) and is held every January. AVING NEWS has reported the most news on CES, MWC, and IFA, the world's three major tech exhibitions for the past 13 years. It is sending special reporters to CES this year to report major issues in the global market and introduce outstanding Korean companies to the world.
